newsitem.title: NORWAY: Esso, Enterprise make new N. Sea oil find - report.
newsitem.headline: Esso, Enterprise make new N. Sea oil find - report.

text.p: Esso Exploration and Enterprise Oil have made a new oil discovery in block 25/10-8 in the North Sea, the daily Stavanger Aftenbladet said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said the find, which is tentatively known as Hanz, was believed to be "rather large."

A spokeswoman at the Norwegian Oil Directorate, which is charged with releasing all information about exploration on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, said an announcement would be made in the next day or so.

Stavanger Aftenbladet said the well was drilled by Deepsea Trym and the testing was so positive that the rig has already begun a so-called side-track well, which could show an even larger oil formation.
The first discovery could be developed via subsea tie back to Esso's production ship at the Balder field, 15 km southwest of Hanz, it said.

But if the side-track well, which will be drilled to a depth of 2,500 metres below sea level, reveals what geologists believe is there, the discovery could be in the order of 200 million barrels, Stavanger Aftenbladet said.
In that instance the find would be in the same class as the Jotun find, made by the same two companies with Esso as operator, the newspaper said.
